title: Gold Slips Below $4,400 as Rising Oil Prices and Treasury Yields Squeeze Bullion
excerpt: Iran's shift to an offensive military posture and firmer U.S. yields pressure gold ahead of the Fed's July meeting minutes on Wednesday.
body:
• Spot gold fell 0.5% to \$4,391 per ounce on Tuesday, pressured by rising U.S. Treasury yields and higher oil prices driven by Iran's shift to an offensive military posture.
  • Oil prices spiked after Iran declared it would adopt a "fully offensive" stance following the collapse of ceasefire negotiations with the United States.
  • Markets are pricing a nearly 65% chance the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in September, after weaker-than-expected jobs data and cooling inflation.
  • Investors are watching for the Fed's July meeting minutes, due Wednesday, and Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks at Jackson Hole for clues on the rate outlook.

Gold retreated on Tuesday as rising U.S. Treasury yields and a surge in oil prices weighed on the non-yielding metal, while traders positioned ahead of the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes for direction on interest rates.

Where Prices Stand

Spot gold was down 0.5% at \$4,391.14 per ounce as of early trading, while U.S. gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.6% to \$4,446.70, according to Reuters. The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield extended gains, raising the opportunity cost of holding bullion.

Silver slipped 1% to \$65.11 per ounce, platinum fell 1.2% to \$1,748.56, and palladium declined 1.2% to \$1,317.01 in a broad metals retreat.

Iran Escalation Lifts Oil, Pressures Gold

Oil prices edged higher after Iran declared it would shift to a "fully offensive" military posture following the breakdown of negotiations aimed at ending the war with the United States. Washington ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement, raising the prospect of renewed hostilities.

Elevated energy prices tend to stoke inflationary fears and bolster expectations that the Fed may need to keep interest rates higher for longer. While gold is traditionally viewed as an inflation hedge, higher rates diminish the appeal of non-yielding assets like bullion.

"Oil prices will remain one of the key factors keeping gold under pressure as the situation in the Middle East continues to look uncertain."

— Soni Kumari, ANZ analyst

Fed Minutes and the Rate Debate

The release of the Fed's July meeting minutes on Wednesday is this week's most closely watched event. Markets are also looking ahead to Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks at the Jackson Hole economic symposium for signals on whether the central bank is leaning toward another rate hike or an extended pause.

The rate outlook has shifted meaningfully in recent weeks. Market pricing for a September quarter-point hike has flipped to a nearly 65% probability of a hold, driven by unexpected job losses in July, lower-than-expected consumer price inflation, and weaker retail sales data.

Still, some Fed officials remain hawkish. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack recently reiterated the case for raising rates "right now" to tame persistent inflation, setting up a potential clash at the central bank's next meeting.

Gold's Month in Context

Despite Tuesday's pullback, gold has rallied more than 10% in August, recovering sharply from the selloff triggered by the Iran war's market disruption. Analysts at MUFG noted that "gold has nevertheless remained supported by renewed investor demand and stronger central-bank purchases, particularly from China."

Technical analysts at Reuters see support at \$4,381, with a break below potentially opening a path toward the \$4,320 to \$4,351 range.

What to Watch

For investors, the near-term trajectory hinges on three factors: the tone of the Fed minutes, the direction of oil prices as the Iran conflict evolves, and whether incoming economic data continues to support the case for a rate pause. Gold's 9% August rally was driven largely by Chinese and retail buying. Whether that demand holds through a period of rising yields will determine if the metal can sustain levels above \$4,400.
